newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank/Portugal could cut key rate Monday - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Bank/Portugal could cut key rate Monday - analysts.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal could cut its key draining rate, the rate at which it absorbs excess liquidity, by 15 to 30 basis points on Monday, some analysts said.
Others felt the central bank could opt to wait until it had a clearer idea on what would be the outcome of 1997 public sector wage negotiations before acting.
The Bank of Portugal will set reserve conditions for the next commercial bank accounting period at 1415 GMT on Monday.
The Bank's draining rate has stood at 6.8 percent since April 19. The repo rate was eased 10 basis points to 7.0 percent on October 21.

"The inflation figures for October were well received by the markets, but I think the Bank is going to wait for the government to define its wages policy more clearly," said Banco Finantia's Isabel Costa.
"It may cut the draining rate 0.125 percentage points, but the Bank has shown itself to be very cautious," said Joao Miguel Lourenco of Lisbon broker Siemca.
Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) economist Rui Martins dos Santos saw the possibility of a 25-30 basis point cut in the draining rate and a 15 basis point cut in the repo rate.
All analysts said there was room for a cut. The only question was whether the Bank would make use of it.
Better-than-expected inflation figures for October had increased the Bank's room for manoeuvre, analysts said.

In October, inflation dipped 0.1 percent month-on-month which brought the year-on-year rate to three percent, while the 12-month rolling average, the government's benchmark, eased to 3.2 percent from 3.3 percent in September.
But the prices' index is likely to edge higher again at the end of the year for statistical reasons. Month-on-month inflation was very low at the end of last year.
